texts.preamble: Sachin Mittal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 October, 2025 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:27483 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajesh Kumar Gupta On The 30th Of October, 2025 Misc. Criminal Case No. 15529 of 2023 Sachin Mittal Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh Appearance: Shri Sanjay Kumar Bahirani - Advocate for the petitio Shri Vikram Pippal - Pl for the State. Order
texts.facts: The present petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the petitioner seeking quashment of Crime No.383/2019 registered at Police Station Ambah, District Morena for offence punishable under Sections 420, 272, 273, 120-B of IPC and Sections 51 and 59 of Food Safety Act and all consequential proceedings. 2. The prosecution case, in short is that , as per the prosecution story on 01.08.2019 food safety officer Rekha Soni submitted one written letter for registration of FIR alleging that on 30.07.2019, one go-down of co-accused Sunil Agarwal behind the Jai Ambe Garden was sealed by her. Thereafter, on 31.07.2019 Rekha Soni/food safety officer and other food safety officer-Anil Pratap Singh Parishar and Tehsildar Ramnivas Sharma & Ors unlocked the said go-down of co-accused Sunil Agarwal and during inspection 1153 bags of Dexotrin powder and six iron drums which were filled with RM Chemical NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27483 2 MCRC-15529-2023 were kept in the go-down. Thereafter, the inspecting authorities had drawn the sample and of Dexotrin powder and RM chemical in absence of co- accused Sunil Agarwal. The aforesaid samples had been sent to the food laboratory Bhopal for testing so, it was alleged that co-accused Sunil Agarwal had stored the Malto Dexotin powder and RM chemical for promoting the food adulteration business and further alleged that the co- accused is gaining illegal advantage and such business which is harmful for the health of general public. During investigation of the case one written letter has been submitted to police authority by food safety officer Rekha Soni on 14-10-2019, in which it has been alleged that on 27-9-2019 Mittal laboratory and chemical supplier has been inspected by food and administrative department at the time of checking, petitioner was present who stated that he sells machinery equipment and chemicals and same was stored Sachin Mittal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47124589/ 1 thereafter, inspecting team perused the document which were available at petitioner's premises and authority had got the knowledge that proprietor of said firm sold the Malto dexotin powder, skimmed milk powder and RM chemical, hydrogen peroxide, reji, refined palm oil and other substance which were used for adulterant milk thus, however, no such article which mention hereinabove have been found in petitioner premises, only bills of the applicant's firm were seized therefore, the applicant has been arrayed as an accused in the offence by alleging that the applicant helped to the co-accused in his business of chemical for promoting the adulterated milk and except such things there was no iota of evidence available with the inspecting authority by which in any manner the applicant could be dragged NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27483 3 MCRC-15529-2023 in the offence. The investigation against the present applicant was pending, therefore, charge sheet has been filed only against the co-accused. 3 . From perusal of the GST registration as well as shop act license of the applicant and name of the applicant firm itself reflect that the applicant is running the business as chemical supplier and under any law no restriction has been imposed by legislature to sell the chemical and dexotrin powder and since beginning authority was very well aware that applicant is selling the chemical and other food products. In the entire FIR, no consumer has made any complaint that the applicant is selling the said product for adulterating the food articles, even no food articles were found from the applicants premises but in spite of this the shameful action has been taken by the officer just under the pressure of police whereas, they were not having any iota of evidence which restricted to the applicant for selling the chemicals and dexotrin powder to the shopkeepers and consumers. 4 . There is no allegation leveled against the present applicant in the entire FIR, nor the name of applicant has been reflected but during investigation on seizing the bill of applicant's firm, he has been arrayed as an accused whereas main allegation for storage of chemicals is against co- accused Sunil Agarwal that being so, in view of the above reasons applicant deserves to be exonerated from the allegation leveled against him.
texts.arguments: 5 . It has been alleged against the applicant that he sells the chemical and other substance in the market and which is offence u/s 272,273 and 420 of IPC. Approach of the inspecting authority is highly misconceived and shameful because once the applicant has obtained his registration under the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27483 4 MCRC-15529-2023 GST for selling chemical and other substance and not only he is authorized to sell the chemical but also his firm has been registered in the name of Mittal Laboratory and Chemical Supplier then in such circumstances if any restriction was made by the Legislature, then definitely registration of the applicant firm would not have been made by the GST Department in their records. Even otherwise, the applicant is having a shop act registration which issued by the concerning department in the name of Mittal Laboratory and chemical Supplier thus, applicant can trade the business of those substances which are added in the food. In spite of this why the applicant has been prosecuted, is not understandable. The action taken by the inspecting authority as well as the police seems to be prima facie illegal, arbitrary and violation of article 14 and 19 (1) G of the Constitution of India. In such circumstances strict direction is required to be issued against the respondent department and against the police authority. The same matter has been considered by this court in the case of Balmukund Gard Vs. State of M.P. vide order dated 23.11.2019 passed in M.Cr.C. No.39005/2019. Sachin Mittal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47124589/ 2 6 . Learned counsel for petitioner also placed reliance on the judgements passed in the case of Shambudayal vs. State_of Gujarat 2003 FAJ 94, and Jitendra Kumar vs. State of Punjab 2008(2) FAC 437 and Ajit Kumar Sangwi V/s State of M.P. and Vinay S/oAshok Goyal V/s State of M.P. MCRC No.40446/2021. 7 . Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that the petitioner has approached this Court invoking its inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C., contending that the FIR and consequent proceedings are NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27483 5 MCRC-15529-2023 malicious, frivolous and an abuse of process of law. It is submitted that the alleged offences under the Food Safety and Standards Act are compoundable and triable by a designated authority and the invocation of IPC provisions is unwarranted. It is further submitted that that no direct evidence connects the petitioner with adulteration or misbranding and continuation of proceedings would cause irreparable harm to his reputation and business. Hence, he prays that petition be allowed and the FIR registered at Crime No.383/2019 at Police Station Ambah, District Morena for offence punishable under Sections 420, 272, 273, 120-B of IPC and Sections 51 and 59 of Food Safety Act and all consequential proceedings be [LEAKAGE_MASK] regarding the present petitioner. 8. Learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, opposed the petition by submitting that the allegations reveal a systematic and deliberate act of preparing and selling adulterated spurious milk, which is dangerous to public health. It is further submitted that the acts of deception and misrepresentation fall squarely under Section 420 IPC and the presence of conspiracy and adulteration attracts the provisions of Sections 272, 273, and 120-B IPC, in addition to the statutory offences under the Food Safety and Standards Act. Hence, the proceedings cannot be [LEAKAGE_MASK] at the threshold. 16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27483 7 MCRC-15529-2023 [(1992) Supp (1) SCC 335] has categorically laid down the parameters under which the High Court may exercise its inherent powers to quash criminal proceedings. The Court held that such power should be invoked only where the allegations do not disclose any cognizable offence, are absurd or inherently improbable, or where proceedings are manifestly attended with malafide intention.
